name: Reference soil Kenya 67
summary: Grassland soil on weathered volcanic rock in the Kenyan highlands. A black, humus-rich topsoil sits over a clay subsoil that cracks as it dries, with calcium carbonate concretions accumulating below about 70 cm.

info.Vegetation: Natural grassland dominated by Themeda triandra

credit: Photo: ISRIC World Soil Reference Collection, CC BY-SA 3.0 https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:ISRIC_monolith_KE-067.jpg — Site and horizon data condensed from ISRIC – World Soil Information https://isis.isric.org/monoliths/reference-soil-ke067 — Feature notes written for this site.

horizons.name: Ah
horizons.description: Black (7.5YR 2/0 moist) silty clay; strong fine and medium crumb structure; friable; many very fine roots; non-calcareous; gradual smooth boundary.

horizons.name: AB
horizons.description: Black (2.5Y 2/0 moist) silty clay; strong fine and medium crumb and fine subangular blocky structure; friable; many very fine roots; non-calcareous; clear wavy boundary.

horizons.name: Bth
horizons.description: Black clay; strong medium prismatic parting to fine and medium angular blocky structure; firm; continuous thin clay–humus cutans on ped faces; moderately calcareous; gradual smooth boundary.

horizons.name: Bt
horizons.description: Very dark gray (2.5Y 3/0 moist) clay; strong very coarse prismatic structure; firm; continuous moderately thick clay cutans on ped faces; moderately calcareous; gradual smooth boundary.

horizons.name: Bci
horizons.description: Very dark gray (10YR 3/1 moist) clay; moderate coarse angular blocky structure; friable; patchy slickensides; moderately calcareous; clear smooth boundary.

horizons.name: Ckc1
horizons.description: Dark grayish brown (2.5Y 4/2 moist) clay; weakly coherent massive parting to fine subangular blocky structure; friable; very few soft carbonate concretions; moderately calcareous; gradual smooth boundary.

horizons.name: Ckc2
horizons.description: Dark grayish brown (2.5Y 4/2 moist) clay; massive parting to fine subangular blocky structure; friable; very few soft carbonate concretions; moderately calcareous; gradual smooth boundary.

horizons.name: Ckc3
horizons.description: Weak red (2.5YR 4/2 moist) sandy clay loam; weakly coherent massive; friable; common large hard carbonate concretions; strongly calcareous.

features.title: Grass tussock
features.description: Base of a Themeda triandra tussock. Dense grass roots supply the organic matter that makes the topsoil black.

features.title: Crumb structure
features.description: Small rounded aggregates formed by fine roots and soil fauna, typical of grassland topsoils.

features.title: Root
features.description: A root crossing the Bth horizon. Roots grow along the ped faces, where the clay–humus coatings are.

features.title: Horizontal crack
features.description: A shrinkage crack near the Bt/Bci boundary. In this clay, cracks open when it dries and close when it is wet.

features.title: Vertical crack
features.description: A wide crack between prisms. Surface material can fall in during the dry season, slowly mixing the profile (vertic behavior).

features.title: Carbonate specks
features.description: White specks of secondary calcium carbonate. Water rarely percolates deeper in this climate, so dissolved carbonate precipitates here.

features.title: Soft carbonate concretion
features.description: Soft, powdery calcium carbonate. It would fizz with 1 M HCl.

features.title: Carbonate-cemented zone
features.description: Pale zone where carbonate coats and cements fragments of weathered rock.

features.title: Hard carbonate concretions
features.description: Large, hard carbonate concretions, typical of the strongly calcareous Ckc3 horizon.
